main_body: White porcelain bathtub seen from above, with a blue water surface inside, a white front rim and a thin grey front face on two small golden feet
top_band: Column scan: rows 3-4 are a light rim (L 236/201), row 5 is a darker blue back inner wall, rows 6-9 are the water surface, and rows 10-11 are the white front rim (L 228). The whole top reads as about 9 rows, rows 3-11.
evidence: The opening is clearly shown: the water surface is visible between the back and front rims (rows 5-9). But the vertical south face is only 2 rows (12-13, L 201 to 164) plus the small feet. The top and opening take about 9 of roughly 13 body rows, so the drawing reads mostly as a top-down plan with a thin front strip. The front face has no eave shadow (it only fades from 201 to 164) and no inset detail. The front face is too thin to count as a real south face, so the 3/4 construction is not met. Failing under the strict rule.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours in total, against 38-40 for the references, and 10 colours per tile against 17-20. The ramps are shallow: white, light grey and grey for porcelain, and two blues for water. There is no texture, grain or speckle, and the water is flat bands. The outline is a soft grey-lavender and is not neutral black (0% neutral), so it is acceptable, but the piece looks flatter and thinner than the stall and well references.
